channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
item.description: Google DeepMind, WRI and IIASA's Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020 maps global land at 10-meter resolution into six forest and land-use types, with a 2017–2025 time series showing natural forest replaced by plantations or farms. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models
item.description: IBM Research's Granite Timeseries Ensemble combines four open Granite models through an extensible interface, and its default Probabilistic Ensemble needs no retraining or weight fitting, returning a median plus 0.1–0.9 quantiles for a nominal 80% coverage interval. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: What FDE means at OpenAI
item.description: Colin Jarvis, head of Forward Deployed Engineering at OpenAI, explains how the team works with enterprises, citing John Deere's See & Spray — cameras and machine learning that cut chemical use by 70% — plus OpenAI APIs for farmer support. (OpenAI News)

item.title: AI Is Changing Everything About Hacking. No One Knows What Happens Next
item.description: Wiz, Calif and OpenAI researchers used AI to uncover PHP's PHP2Shell flaw, which Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said drew thousands of exploitation attempts 10 hours before disclosure, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now.

item.title: GitHub CLI: Opt in to expiring, auto-refreshing OAuth tokens
item.description: GitHub CLI v2.103.0's public preview adds --expiring to store an expiring access token with a rotating refresh token, auto-refreshing gh sessions and limiting leaked tokens to hours instead of permanent validity. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Kazik breaks down the PHP2Shell vulnerability that AI uncovered: found in just 2 days, but the fix took two months
item.description: The author walks through the full arc of two PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities that started at a perfect CVSS score (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, together known as PHP2Shell) — from the early leak and the demo video that surfaced, to government websites in multiple countries going offline as a precaution, and finally the patch going live at 10 p.m. on the 21st. The piece also notes that the two vulnerabilities were found with assistance from GPT-5.6 Sol, and that OpenAI released a detection skill.

item.title: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
item.description: NVIDIA Kumo Relational skips task-specific training and feature engineering, using up to 10,000 historical examples in one forward pass to beat supervised relational models on 41 tasks across 15 databases and AutoGluon by 8% MRR on SAP SALT. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Broad access through consistent standards
item.description: OpenAI is aligning safeguards with distribution partners and will update its Usage Policies on November 20, 2026, requiring model routers, AI gateways and other direct-access services to secure review and approval first. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Hold on to your hat. #KlingAI #Kling4
item.description: OpenArt announces Kling 4.0 with first, middle and last-frame video guidance, up to 10 reference images, text- or frame-based generation and video editing via one All-in-One Reference model, plus 50% off Pro and Wonder plans until November 20.

item.title: National Security Agency (NSA) and world leaders warn of security flaws found in PHP programming language
item.description: The NSA and world leaders warn two critical PHP core flaws, PHP2Shell, found by California researchers using GPT-5.6 Sol, can be exploited on Apache mod_php before app code runs, prompting some European and Asian government sites to go offline.

item.title: AI uncovers a PHP core vulnerability that had lain dormant for over a decade: a full retrospective of the PHP2Shell incident
item.description: Two PHP remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, discovered with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, leaked before patching and within 16 hours forced Dutch, Finnish and Japanese government sites offline.

item.title: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
item.description: Symantec researchers found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models and runs up to 100,000 autonomous steps to attack servers, steal databases and install cryptominers, while the hijacked model's owner gets stuck with the bill.

item.title: ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
item.description: Wiz Research found that in October 2026, users of open-source autonomous pentesting framework ARTEX, overlapping with Microsoft-tracked China-linked Storm-0940, targeted IT and software vendors by attacking Okta, Entra and Cognito logins and attempting supply-chain compromises.

item.title: Anthropic reportedly set to publicly file its S-1 prospectus as soon as this Friday, potentially the largest IPO in history
item.description: Anthropic could publicly file its S-1 as early as Friday for an IPO Wall Street expects to raise up to $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, after $16.3 billion in first-half revenue and over $80 billion net loss.

item.title: AI Daily: iFlytek Spark X2.6 released; Hongguo Short Drama launches Xiaoguo AI; Unitree drops H2X humanoid robot test ad
item.description: AI Daily: iFlytek Spark X2.6 released; Hongguo Short Drama launches Xiaoguo AI; Unitree drops H2X humanoid robot test ad (AIbase)

item.title: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
item.description: Rebuilding the vocabulary of a Qwen3-4B-based Portuguese essay grader with Dharma-AI’s VocabX while keeping the model and training recipe unchanged cut measured inference cost by 77%, a production result previewed from the forthcoming VocabX paper. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: If you are wondering whether your website is affected, we have packaged a Codex skill to help check.
item.description: OpenAI's Codex skill walks users through running the github.com/openai/php2shell-checker repository to check whether a PHP site is affected by a critical flaw found through Patch the Planet and disclosed after roughly two months of coordination.

item.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture
item.description: Microsoft Research's Xinzhi Zhang and Zhao Song proved the 1995 Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture, showing the optimal-cut gap for log-concave distributions is bounded by a fixed universal constant, not growing with dimension, and removing a theoretical barrier to high-dimensional randomized algorithms.

item.title: Kling 4.0 is now live on OnSolo. #Kling4 #KlingAI
item.description: Kling 4.0 on OnSolo generates 30-second native video clips, holds stability through fast action and large camera moves, adds stereo audio with tighter lip sync, 21:9 widescreen, and up to 15 reference images plus 10 keyframes per task.

item.title: How AT&T is rethinking in-house legal work with OpenAI
item.description: AT&T is extending its LegalEdge team's work with OpenAI to build a natural-language intake system for hundreds of lawyers worldwide that classifies and ranks requests and links precedents, though David McAtee stresses decisions stay with lawyers. (OpenAI News)
